Order 
This appeal under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellant - Claimant being aggrieved by the award dated 6.9.2022 passed by 4th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur (for short the "Tribunal') in MACC No.3367/2018 (Omkar Vs. Suresh Kumar Maravi and others).

sentences.text: 2. The facts of the case in short are that on the date of incident i.e. on 1.9.2018 deceased Subhash and Smt. Savita along with their relatives were going to Singarpur from village Vikrampur.

Other injured Pawan Kumar along with his father was also travelling on the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:55503 auto bearing registration No. MP-52-R-1383 and was going from Vikrampur to Ghusiya.

The driver of the offending vehicle while driving the auto rashly and negligently dashed both the deceased and resultantly, turned turtle, due to which, both the deceased fell down on the ground and injured Pawan Kumar also sustained severe injuries.

Immediately after the incident, both the deceased were taken to Government Hospital, Dindori for treatment, from where, they were shifted to Medical Hospital, Jabalpur but unfortunately, on the way to Medial Hospital, Jabalpur, they died.

Whereas, injured Pawan was got admitted in Government Hospital,
Vikrampur where primary treatment was given to him.
Thereafter, he took treatment in Sudha Hospital, Jabalpur.

On the basis of information, Crime No. 139/18 for offence under Sections 279,
337, 338 and 304-A of IPC was registered at Police Station Shahpura, District Dindori.

Learned counsel for the appellant / claimant submits that deceased Master Subhash, aged about 3 years, was the only son of the appellant who died in the accident took place on 1.9.2018, for which,
the appellant filed a claim case before the learned Claims Tribunal.
Further, it has been contended that the learned Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.3,77,000/-.

4. Per-contra, learned counsel for respondents supported the impugned award passed by learned Claims Tribunal and contended that NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:55503 no additional amount is required to be enhanced in favour of the appellant.

5. Heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the record thoroughly.
6.
On perusal of the record, it is evident that Master Subhash was aged about 3 years at the time of accident and he was only son of the appellant / claimant.

On considering the age of the deceased Master Subhash and also taking into consideration loss of love and affection and future prospectus of the deceased, it would be appropriate to enhance the amount of compensation on lump sum basis including the amount already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.

7. Learned counsel for the appellant / claimant has fairly conceded that the appeal is valued for Rs.2,00,000/- (Rs. Two lacs only) and accordingly, Court fee has been paid Rs.5000/-.
8.
Accordingly, the appellant / claimant is held entitled for enhancement of Rs.1,23,000/- in addition to the amount already awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.
9. With aforesaid enhancement in the amount of compensation, the appeal is finally disposed of.
